🌙 ⭐ ✨ A Dedication

The Fairy Garden of Love

A poem for Fairy

Beneath the moonlight

and under the willow

but next to the castle

as it glistens...

You built a castle.

A story.

A heart out of kindness.

You gave a turtle magic,

made an invisible friend visible

so she'd never be alone.

You let a little girl be a princess

and held a hand that needed holding

all the way through every wood.

Thank you for being her rainbow.

Thank you for the fairyland.

Thank you for being you.

✦ ✦ ✦

Imagined & Created by Boat Momma, who loves Andy and the Princess Lauren who loves her favorite Fairy

We love you, big.

He is one in the same,
a million to one &
one in a million.

✨ ⭐ ✦ Chapter One

There Once Was a Fairy Dairy Fairy

Fairy hovers above his great Australian castle, wand aglow with evening light.

Once upon a time, in the wide and wondrous land of Australia, there lived a very special fairy. His name was Fairy... Fairy the Fairy Dairy Fairy... and he was not quite like any other fairy in the world.

He lived in a magnificent castle that rose up from the green hills of fairyland, its towers catching the last light of every sunset and the first gold of every morning. From the highest window, Fairy could see for ever and ever... past the glittering streams, past the whispering meadows, all the way to where the sky kissed the earth good night.

Fairy had silver-blue wings that caught the moonlight when he flew, and a wand that had been known to scatter the most lovely sparks across the evening sky... tiny golden dots that the animals of fairyland called "Fairy's breadcrumbs," because they always led somewhere wonderful.

🐢 ✦ Chapter Two

The Castle & the Magic Turtle Madge

✏️ Illustrated by Lauren Elizabeth... Madge the Magical Turtle, with BoRo the Fairy riding on her back.

Fairy's castle was not a cold or lonely place. Oh no. It was full of warmth and wonder, from the ivy-covered towers to the glowing lanterns that lit themselves every evening without being asked.

And in the castle garden, beside the clearest little pond you ever saw, lived Madge.

Madge was a turtle... but not an ordinary turtle. Madge was a magic turtle, and she had a shell the colour of deep moss and eyes that seemed to hold tiny stars inside them. She moved slowly and deliberately, the way that truly wise turtles do, and Fairy trusted her above almost anyone else in all of fairyland.

When Fairy was troubled, he would sit beside Madge at the pond's edge, and she would simply blink her ancient eyes... once, twice... and somehow everything felt a little easier. Madge didn't speak in words. She spoke in stillness, and Fairy understood her perfectly.

Sometimes, late at night, a soft green glow would rise from her shell and drift upward like wishes, lighting the castle courtyard with colours that had no names. The other creatures of fairyland would come to watch, sitting quietly together, and Fairy would smile the private smile of someone who knows exactly how lucky he is.

🍦 ✨ 🍝 Chapter Two and a Half

Patience, Kindness, and Ice Cream

Fairy was very good at being a fairy, but Fairy was even better at teaching. He taught patience by waiting for the slowest snail in fairyland to cross the path, never once rushing it. He taught kindness by sharing his ice cream with anyone who looked like they needed a scoop more than he did, even when it was the very last one in the bowl.

And most importantly, Fairy taught that laughter is a kind of magic all its own... the kind that doesn't need a wand at all.

Princess Lauren liked to test this theory often. "What if I dropped my ice cream? On purpose?" she'd ask, eyes very serious.

"Then we would share mine," Fairy would say, and they'd both laugh until their sides hurt, which, it turns out, is also a very good use of an afternoon.

Now, Fairy loved ice cream more than almost anyone in fairyland understood. He loved good food in general... pasta most of all, twirled up high on a fork, and purple pickles, which nobody else in fairyland would even try, but Fairy thought were simply delicious and refused to apologize for it.

He loved games too... the kind you could win, which felt wonderful, and just as much, the kind you could lose, which felt almost as good once you got the hang of laughing about it. And he loved music, good music, the real stuff... never country, and never, under any circumstances, Boat Momma's singing.

💎 ✦ Chapter Three

DanDan, the Best Invisible Friend

DanDan?

DanDan's presence fills the gem-lit cave... invisible, but oh-so-very-there.

Now, Fairy also had a best friend named DanDan.

The funny thing about DanDan was that you couldn't see him. Not even a little bit... not even if you squinted, or looked sideways, or held a prism up to the light. DanDan was invisible from the top of his head to the tips of his toes, and he had been that way always, and he didn't mind it one bit.

What DanDan loved, more than almost anything in the world, was gems. He collected them everywhere he went... deep red rubies, sky-blue sapphires, pale green emeralds, and ones that had no name at all, that simply caught the light and held it there like a secret. His collection was legendary in fairyland, even though you couldn't see the collector.

DanDan also loved waterfalls... the thunder and the mist of them, the way they made the world feel washed clean. And he loved caves, those quiet dark places where the gems grew slowly in the rock, where echoes lived, where you could sit and listen to the deep hum of the earth and feel very small and very safe at the same time.

When Fairy flew into a cave with DanDan, he always knew exactly where his friend was... because the gems would glitter a little brighter, just there, right beside him. That is the kind of friend DanDan was.

🌸 💖 Chapter Four

Princess Lauren & the LittleLove

Princess Lauren reaches for Fairy's hand as LittleLove peeks from behind the tree.

And then there was Princess Lauren.

Oh, Princess Lauren. Fairy loved her the way the moon loves the tide... constantly, without even trying, pulled always in her direction. She had a crown that caught the light on mornings and a laugh that the butterflies came to listen to. She lived in the most beautiful part of fairyland, where the flowers bloomed in colours that didn't have names yet, and wherever she walked, the grass stood up a little straighter, as if pleased she had passed.

When Fairy and Princess Lauren walked together through the meadows, she always wanted to hold his hand. She would reach out... and Fairy's heart would do a small, private leap... and they would walk that way, hand in hand, through the winding paths of fairyland while the trees nodded and the birds grew quiet to watch.

Now, Fairy also had his very own LittleLove... a small, shy, luminous little thing that belonged entirely to him and to no one else. LittleLove had a habit of hiding behind trees whenever Princess Lauren was near, peeking out with enormous soft eyes, and scurrying back if anyone looked too directly.

But when Princess Lauren held Fairy's hand? LittleLove would watch from behind the bark... and perhaps smile, just a little.

🎈 🎮 🎵 Chapter Four and a Half

The Things Fairy Loves

Fairy loved a great many things, and he was not shy about it.

He loved balloons, the kind that bob just slightly out of reach until somebody jumps for them. He loved games... especially the kind you could win, and just as much, the kind you could lose, because losing spectacularly and laughing about it after is its own small art form.

He loved music. Good music. Real good music... never country, and absolutely never Princess Lauren's momma's singing (sorry, Boat Momma, but everyone agrees).

And he loved, more than almost anything, the quiet moment when Princess Lauren reached over and held his hand without being asked.

"You don't have to ask," she told him once. "I'm always going to hold it."

And Fairy believed her completely, because Princess Lauren never said a single thing she didn't mean.

⚠️ 🌿 Chapter Five

The Rules of the Woods

!
YELLOW
WOODS

Fairy stands firm at the border... the safe Green Woods on the left, the forbidden Yellow Woods to the right.

Now, every fairyland has its rules. And Fairy knew the rules of this fairyland very well.

There were two kinds of woods.

⚠ The Yellow Woods... Stay Out

Deep in the east of fairyland grew the Yellow Woods, and they were to be avoided. The trees there grew too close together and blocked out the friendly sky. The paths wound in circles that led nowhere good, and the shadows moved in ways that shadows should not move. Nobody could tell you exactly what lived in the Yellow Woods, because those who had ventured in had always come back quieter than before, and unwilling to speak of it. Fairy never went there. Not once. Not ever.

🌿 The Green Woods... Tread Carefully

The Green Woods were not dangerous, exactly... but they were wise. They gave warnings. A branch might brush your cheek with particular firmness. A bird might call in a pattern that made you think twice. The wind changed direction in a meaningful way. If you paid attention to the Green Woods, they would look after you. If you didn't pay attention, that was your own business, and the Green Woods would not be held responsible. Always listen in the Green Woods.

Fairy made sure Princess Lauren knew these rules too. He told them to DanDan, and to Madge (who blinked solemnly), and to LittleLove (who listened from behind a tree).

🌈 The Rainbow Woods... These Are Love

And then there are the Rainbow Woods. All the colours of the rainbow live there, side by side, and they are how Fairy loves... wide and bright and every colour at once, none of them cancelling the others out. The Rainbow Woods are the most beautiful place in all of fairyland. Now, you do not go into the Yellow Woods or the Green Woods alone. But here is the thing about all of it... if you hold Fairy's hand, you will be okay. The Yellow will not trick you. The Green will only warn you gently. And the Rainbow will wrap itself all the way around you both.

🦐 ✨ 🫖 Chapter Five and a Half

Seita, the Pet Prawn

Not everyone in fairyland was a fairy, a turtle, or invisible. Some of fairyland's most important residents were, in fact, prawns.

Fairy had a pet prawn named Seita, who lived in a teacup by the castle window and had opinions about absolutely everything, though nobody could quite understand prawn, so his opinions remained mostly a mystery to everyone but Fairy.

Seita disliked Tuesdays for reasons of his own. He loved warm water. And he once startled an entire dinner party by doing a small, dramatic flip that nobody had asked for and everybody applauded anyway.

Fairy adored him completely and would not hear a single word against him.

The Music of Fairyland

♪
♫
♪
♫
♪

Fairy conducts the music of fairyland... and the whole kingdom listens.

There was one more very important thing about fairyland: its music.

Fairyland had magnificent music. It rose from everywhere at once... from the waterfall where DanDan loved to sit, from the humming of Madge's shell, from the wind as it braided itself through the treetops. The creatures played instruments that looked like nothing you'd find in any shop, and when they all played together, the sound was something you could feel in your chest like warmth.

🎵 A Note on the Music of Fairyland

Fairyland has no country music. This is not because country music is bad, exactly... it is simply that fairyland runs on a different frequency. The music here is good music: music that makes the flowers lean toward the sound, that makes the gems in DanDan's collection vibrate faintly with recognition, that makes Madge blink with slow approval, that makes Princess Lauren tip her head sideways as though hearing something she has always known. There is plenty of it, and all of it is good, and if you listen carefully enough, it seems to know your name.

Fairy loved this music deeply. The good stuff. Not Princess Lauren's momma's singing. He would sometimes fly upward into the evening sky, high above the castle towers, and simply float there... wings spread wide, eyes closed... while the music of fairyland rose up to meet him, and the stars came out one by one above his head.

And LittleLove, watching from behind a tree far below, would glow just faintly with a light it couldn't explain.

🔐 💖 ✨ Chapter Six and a Half

Locks, Who Loves the Castle

Fairy's best friend was named Locks. Locks was also, confusingly, a Lauren... but there could only be one Princess Lauren in all of fairyland, so Locks went by Locks instead, and never once complained about it.

Locks was beautiful. Genuinely, properly beautiful, in the way that made fairyland creatures stop and look twice. But Locks was not a princess, and never wished to be one, because fairyland already had exactly the princess it needed, and Locks was perfectly happy being something else entirely... something all her own.

Locks loved the castle completely, every stone and stair and window of it, mostly because LittleLove lived there too, small and shy and glowing behind whichever tree was closest.

Locks and LittleLove had a whole world together that belonged only to them. They counted the trees in the courtyard. They counted the stairs up every tower, twice, just to be sure. They counted the music notes that drifted up from fairyland in the evenings, though they always lost count somewhere around fifty and simply started again, laughing.

All of this happened quietly, while Fairy was busy with Fairy duties... which were many, and important, and occasionally involved a prawn.

"Who keeps count of all of it when I'm not looking?" Fairy asked once.

Locks smiled. "Who else," she said, "is going to guard the castle? Besides the locks?"

Fairy blinked. "The door locks?"

"No," said Locks, still smiling. "Me. I'm the locks. Keep up."

It remains, to this day, fairyland's most confusing joke, and also one of its best.

🌙 ⭐ ✨ The Last Page

And So It Was, Every Evening in Fairyland

DanDan…?

Hand in hand beneath the Australian stars... Fairy, Princess Lauren, and all who are loved in fairyland.

And so, every evening in fairyland, this is how things were:

Fairy the Fairy Dairy Fairy flew home to his great Australian castle as the sky turned the colours of a fire's last hour. Madge waited by the pond, her ancient eyes full of quiet things. DanDan was somewhere nearby... you could tell by the way the gems glittered for no particular reason, just a little too brightly, right over there. Princess Lauren's hand found Fairy's hand on the path between the Rainbow Woods and the castle gate, and they walked that way, quietly, listening to the music of fairyland rising around them.

💛 ✨ 🩹 Chapter Seven and a Half

When Fairy Got Sick

One evening, Fairy did not feel like flying. His wings hung a little heavy, and the music of fairyland sounded far away, even though it was playing right where it always played. Fairy was sick, and everybody could tell, because Fairy without his sparkle is a very different kind of quiet.

Princess Lauren did not panic. She simply sat beside him and told him that she knew spells. Real ones. The kind only a princess is allowed to know.

"Spells aren't always in fairy language," she explained, very seriously. "Sometimes they're in other languages. That's how you know they're strong."

And so, very carefully, she said them, one at a time, in whatever language felt right for each one:

Je t'aime jusqu'à la lune et retour.

(I love you to the moon and back.)

Oldhay myay andhay, andway ouyay'llay ebay okay.

(Hold my hand, and you'll be ok.)

Je peux faire de la soupe avec ma maman.

(I can have my momma make soup.)

Ai'llway etgay emsgay orfay ouyay.

(I'll get gems for you.)

Les câlins sont une potion.

(Hugs are a potion.)

Ouyay areay yay favoritefay erspersonay.

(You are my favorite person.)

Je serai toujours là.

(I will always be there.)

Eelfay etterbay owNay.

(Feel better now.)

And Fairy did. Not all at once, and not by magic exactly... but slowly, the way these things actually work, he felt better. Because it turns out the strongest spells were never about the words at all. They were about who was saying them, and why.

👑 ✨ ⭐ A Royal Portrait

Queen Fairy Fairy Dairy Fairy

There is one more thing that must be known about Fairy... something that fairyland whispers only on the quietest nights, when the stars are brightest and even Madge is asleep.

Fairy is not merely a fairy. Fairy is a Queen. The Queen Fairy Fairy Dairy Fairy... crowned in gold, wings spread wide and blue as the deep Australian sky, wand raised and ready, jewels glinting on the royal crown. Regal and wonderful and entirely, perfectly Fairy.

This portrait was painted by the Royal Court Artist... the one and only Lauren Elizabeth... on the occasion of the Queen's coronation, in the grand tradition of fairyland's finest painters. It now hangs in the Great Hall of the castle, where all who enter may admire it.

🎨 ✨ The Royal Gallery

The Fairyland Poles

Deep in the heart of fairyland, lining the royal path that leads from the Green Woods all the way to Fairy's castle gate, stand the Fairyland Poles.

Nobody knows exactly when Lauren Elizabeth decorated them. One morning they were plain cardboard. The next, they were covered in colours and shapes and creatures and the word "Fairy" written in her very own hand, and fairyland was better for it.

✏️ Pole One — triangles, diamonds, swirls, and "Fairy" in Lauren's own writing

✏️ Pole Two — mushrooms, a fairy, trees, and a little blue flower

The Fairy Phone, for calling fairyland direct

Visitors to fairyland are encouraged to look at the poles closely as they pass. Every shape on them means something. The triangle points up toward where good things are. The diamond is for DanDan's gems. The mushrooms are for magic. The flower is for Princess Lauren. And the fairy drawn in pencil, right in the middle of it all, is of course Fairy.

The poles will stand there for ever, or until the cardboard gets soggy, whichever comes first.

⛵ 🌊 ✨ Chapter Eight

Boat Momma Sails Away

And somewhere far off, past the edges of fairyland, where the water turns the colour of a held breath, Boat Momma set sail for a different, far away land.

Not because she had to. Simply because a boat is the sort of thing that always finds its way home eventually, wherever home turns out to be.

Princess Lauren waved from the shore until the boat was nothing but a speck, and then not even that.

Fairy held her hand the entire time.
